Aria: Heads-up: saw a regression on the warmup vs continuation paths after the FP8 kernel selector change.
Aria: Baseline (old selector): warmup TTFT ~95ms, steady TPS 1.6k on A100_80GB with longctx=32k
Aria: After change (auto-int8-fallback for long sequences) warmup TTFT is ~120ms and steady TPS drops to ~1.35k for some workloads.
Sam: Can you paste the profiling slice? scheduler + kernel pick logs?
Aria: Pasting simplified scheduler trace and bench run for a 12k prompt with mixed 4-bit/FP8 layers.
Aria: ```
# scheduler trace (warmup->continuation)
[2056789012] kernel_select: FP8_primary
[2056789013] schedule: microbatch=8 -> launch FP8 kernel (warmup)
[2056789016] kvcache: store chunk(0..4096) fp8
[2056789021] kernel_select: detected long_attn -> switch to INT8_compat_path
[2056789022] dequant: kv_unpack triggered
[2056789024] schedule: microbatch=16 -> launch INT8 kernel (streaming)
```
Aria: Benchbot ran a full sweep, here's the summary (per-run averages):
benchbot: {"run_id":"wvc-2056","model":"redwood-7b-mixq","ctx":12288,"warmup_TTFT_ms":121.3,"steady_TPS":1352,"fallback_rate":0.18}
Marta: 18% fallback rate is pretty high. Do we know why selector flips? calibration skew for some attention layers?
Aria: Looking into calibration table, we see layer-wise scale variance spikes on layers 10-14 when sequence len > 8k. That makes the compat check mark those layers as "unsafe" for FP8 fused-attn and we fall back.
Derek: Could also be KV packing overhead when we store FP8 blocks: unpack+deq on continuation path adds ~6-8ms per microbatch which inflates TTFT if it happens during warmup.
Sam: Is the unpack happening on the critical path for first token? or is it async/IO bound?
Aria: It's on the critical path because we rehydrate KV into GPU workspace before the first decode launch for continuation chunk.
Marta: Two immediate mitigations to test:
- keep FP8 fused-attn for warmup (init pass) even if a few layers flagged, but use safe path for continuation when we know steady state
- change microbatch threshold so continuation uses smaller microbatches to reduce unpack latency spike
Derek: Also consider lazy KV unpack: only unpack first N heads/slices required for the first few decode steps, then stream remaining parts async. That reduces TTFT at cost of more kernel switches.
benchbot: Ran experimental warmup-gate config. Results:
benchbot: {"config":"warmup_gate_v1","ctx":12288,"warmup_TTFT_ms":98.7,"steady_TPS":1420,"fallback_rate":0.06}
Sam: Nice improvement on TTFT and fallback drops. Any quality regressions from warmup gating?
Aria: Quick eval on 500 prompts: no measurable degradation in top-1 output diversity. Calibration test we ran showed transient scale mismatches but they don't affect first token much.
Marta: We should add a guard: only enable warmup gate when fallback_rate > 5% and ctx >= 8k, to avoid unnecessary complexity for small contexts.
Derek: Opening a short RFC for the scheduler change and lazy unpack plan. Also adding a perf test to separate unpack latency from kernel execution.
Aria: RFC link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/412-warmup-gate-kv-lazy-unpack
Sam: I'll pick up a microbenchmark to measure per-layer dequant cost and KV unpack bandwidth. Will post numbers by EOD.
benchbot: Scheduled perf job: job/2056789012-warmup-sweep (ETA ~2h)
Aria: Thanks — let's keep this thread for quick notes. If anyone hits a repro, ping me +Marta.
Aria: :thumbsup:
